content: Live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, may not function effectively when administered concurrently with this medication. This drug is not recommended for use during pregnancy. While there have been reports of harm to infants born to women who used similar drugs, no such reports exist for infants born to women who used amikacin. Amikacin is excreted into breast milk in small amounts. However, many healthcare providers consider breastfeeding safe while using this medication. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications that affect kidney function or hearing may increase the risk of kidney damage or hearing loss when taken with amikacin. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as kidney function tests and amikacin blood levels, may be conducted while you are using this medication. It is important to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, or loss of appetite may occur. Pain, irritation, or redness at the injection site may rarely occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterium called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using amikacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other aminoglycoside antibiotics (such as gentamicin or tobramycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as sulfites), which can cause allergic reactions or other problems.
